manifest.name: dsh-permission-studio
manifest.description: DSH 权限档位工作室：在 Web 设置里按分类、工具、命令、文件路径四层细配权限，支持多档位、会话内切换、拒绝理由引导与工具剔除。

bundle.text:
# dsh-permission-studio bundle patch layer —— 把本插件挂载进 profile 树。
# 依赖宿主侧：@deepseek-ai/dsh-config-editor（写 profile patch）、
# @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver（HTTP 路由）。两者由 dsh-base 默认提供。
- insert:
    - id: dsh-permission-studio
      name: dsh-permission-studio

readme.text: **给 DSH 的权限档位工作室** —— 把「三个固定档位」变成任意多档、每档独立细配、会话内随时切换 分类 · 工具 · 命令 · 文件路径，四层收束，每一条拒绝都能告诉模型该怎么改 [](https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases) [](https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases/latest) [](#开发) [](LICENSE) [中文](README.md) · [English](README.en.md) · [更新日志](CHANGELOG.md) ---

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）自带 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-permission-presets`，提供「任意多个权限档位」和会话内 `/permission` 切换。 但档位表只能手改 YAML，而且粒度只到**沙箱**（`read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`）。 这个插件补上两件事： 1. **一个能点的界面** —— 在 DSH 设置里增删改档位，保存即生效，不用重启 2. **更细的判定** —— 从「整个沙箱开或关」，细化到**哪一类操作、哪一个工具、哪一条命令、哪一个文件** 关键在于：**拒绝不是终点，而是一次说明**。每条规则都能写一句提示词，原样回给模型， 它就知道「这条路不通，换一条」——而不是撞墙重试。
文件规则：同一个模式，读和写可以分别设为允许 / 询问 / 拒绝，拒绝时写自己的提示词

| 层 | 管什么 | 典型用法 | |---|---|---| | **分类规则**（13 类） | 按操作类型批量决定 | 「执行命令一律询问」「读取区外文件一律拒绝」 | | **逐工具覆盖** | 按工具名单独决定，可**剔除** | 「`bash` 从这个会话里彻底消失」 | | **正则规则** | 按工具名 / 命令 / 路径 / 参数匹配 | 「`git push` 必须询问」「`rm -rf` 直接拒绝」 | | **文件规则** | 按文件路径，读和写分别判定 | 「只准改 `docs/**`，`*.env` 一律拒绝」 | 四层从上到下依次检查，命中即定论；**层内多条同时命中时按「拒绝 > 询问 > 允许」取最严**。

<table>
<tr><td width="50%" valign="top">

- 任意多档，每档独立设置沙箱与审批策略
- 显示名、描述、是否设为默认
- 卡片可折叠，头部直接显示「拒绝 N · 询问 M · 共 13 类」
- 每档可选徽标，显示在设置页、原生下拉与档位触发器
13 类操作，每类可设 **询问 / 允许 / 拒绝**： 执行命令 · 读取文件 · 查找文件 · 修改文件 · 读取区外文件 · 写入区外文件 · 读取图片 · 联网访问 · 撤销操作 · 子代理 · 团队协作 · 其他工具 · 重复操作

工具清单来自运行时注册表（全局层 + 所有作用域层的并集），**不是写死的名字**。
每个工具可设为 **跟随分类 / 询问 / 允许 / 拒绝 / 剔除**。

**剔除**不是「调用时拒绝」——它用 DSH 的 `tools.restrict()` 把工具从这个会话的可见清单里真正移除，
模型连它的 schema 都收不到。切换档位时重新计算，先撤销旧限制再施加新的。
按工具名、命令内容、路径或任意参数匹配，动作同样是三态，优先级高于分类与工具覆盖。

readme.section: 文件规则：白名单与黑名单是同一件事
readme.text:
一条规则 = **路径模式 + 读动作 + 写动作 + 可选提示词**。

- 设成「允许」就是白名单，设成「拒绝」就是黑名单，不需要两套东西
- 读写独立判定，**写不隐含读**
- 「未列出的文件」单独一档策略：跟随分类规则（默认，不会把自己锁死）或一律拒绝（纯白名单）
- **列表为空时兜底依然生效**：空表 + 一律拒绝 = 全锁，理由会说明原因
- 界面上有「开启读取 / 开启写入」两个独立开关，缺读、缺写时各出一条提醒

配置页底部有三个按钮：**导出备份 / 导入备份 / 保存全部**。 - 导出得到一个 JSON：全部档位（沙箱、审批、十三类规则、逐工具覆盖、正则规则、文件规则、图标、默认档位）一次带走 - 导出取的是**当前界面状态**，所以先把想改的改完再导出也没问题 - 导入会用它替换当前全部档位配置，内置三档始终保留；写入前会弹确认 - 备份带 `format` 与 `formatVersion`，导入别的 JSON、空文件、来自更高版本的备份都会被拒绝并说明原因

逐工具覆盖：48 个工具动态发现，批量操作，可整条剔除

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add \
  https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases/latest/download/dsh-permission-studio.tgz
```

这个地址永远指向**最新发布版本**。它拿的是 Release 附件里的打包产物，
不是 `main` 分支上还没发布的提交——分支上可能有半成品，发布版不会。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add \
  https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases/download/v0.2.4/dsh-permission-studio.tgz
```

```sh
git clone https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio.git
cd dsh-permission-studio
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "$(pwd)/dsh-permission-studio-0.2.4.tgz"

装完重启 DSH，设置里出现 **权限档位** 一页。

DSH 桌面版的 profile 由 Electron 独占，命令行改不了，要用界面装： **设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**，在「包名或地址」里粘贴： ``` https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases/latest/download/dsh-permission-studio.tgz ``` 这个地址是打包产物（`.tgz` 结尾），安装器会按 tarball 处理，拿到的就是最新发布版本。 **不要填仓库地址**（`https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio`）——那会按 git 源安装， 装的是 `main` 分支当前代码，可能包含还没发布的提交。 > 把 `desktop` 换成你的 profile 名。查看有哪些 profile：`dsh profile list`

**设置里配** → 设置 → 权限档位 → 展开任一档位 **会话里切** → `/permission`（不带参数列出全部档位） ``` /permission 只碰指定文件 ``` 切换当场生效，不用重启。徽标会跟着变，旧档位的图标不会留下来。

徽标直接长在 DSH 原生下拉的图标位置上；内置档位保留自带图标，互不冲突

每条拒绝都能说话。优先级是： ``` 该项自己的理由 > 档位兜底理由 > 分类默认引导语 ``` 兜底理由是**判定时**解析的，不是保存时写死的——所以改一次兜底， 所有没单独填写的项立刻跟着变，不用逐条改。 模型收到的是一句可执行的引导，比如： > 本档位只允许读写文件规则里列出的路径，`src/a.ts` 未被列出。 > 现有规则：`docs/**`(读:allow 写:allow)、`*.md`(读:allow 写:deny)； > 未列出的文件按「一律拒绝」处理。请让用户调整文件规则，或切换到其它档位。
| 内容 | 位置 | |---|---| | 档位表、默认档 | profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`（DSH 原生配置，热重载） | | 分类 / 工具 / 正则 / 文件规则、徽标 | `$DSH_HOME/permission-studio/config.json` | 分开存是有意的：细粒度规则的结构 DSH 不认识，塞进原生配置会触发 schema 校验失败。

```
设置页 iframe ──POST──> /permission-studio/api ──> 写配置 ──> 热重载
                                                        │
会话每次工具调用 ── tools/pre-execute（global 钩子）──> decide()
        ├─ 1. 正则规则（deny > ask > allow）

- 判定 `deny` → 返回 `{ kind: 'deny', reason }`，reason 就是回给模型的话
- 判定 `ask` → 交回 DSH 原生审批，由该档位的审批策略决定是否弹窗
- 插件自身异常 → fail-safe 拒绝本次调用，不放行可疑操作
| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | GET | `/permission-studio/` | 自包含管理页（HTML + CSS + JS 内联） | | GET | `/permission-studio/api` | 档位表、默认档、工具清单、分类枚举 | | POST | `/permission-studio/api` | 保存全部设置 |

```sh npm test # 147 个回归用例 npm pack # 打包 ``` 测试直接调用导出的纯函数（`decide` / `matchFileRule` / `globToRegExp` / `planHiddenTools` / `syncHiddenTools` 等），不需要起服务，秒级跑完。 每个修过的 bug 都留下了对应的回归用例——包括几个不容易想到的： - `restrict` 的限制是取交集累加的，切档不撤销就永远回不去 - 徽标只插不删，切到别的档位会和原生图标并排 - 兜底理由若在保存时物化，改兜底就影响不到已有条目 - 文件规则若把「有规则才生效」写成前提，空列表时兜底等于失效

本插件声明对以下 DSH 宿主版本的兼容（`peerDependencies`）：

| 包 | 兼容区间 |
|---|---|
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `>=4.0.2 <5.0.0` |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer` | `0.2.0-rc.1` · `0.2.0-rc.2` · `0.2.1-rc.1` · `0.2.1-rc.2` |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings` | 同上 |
| `react` / `react-dom` | `^18.2.0` |
| Node.js | `^22.19.0` 或 `>=24.0.0` |

宿主自带的包（cordis、客户端 UI 包）在 profile 里不会被重复安装，
因此这些 peer 声明标为 `optional`——安装时不会报缺失警告，但版本区间仍是明确承诺。

已验证：在干净的 `0.2.1-rc.2` 宿主上安装并启动，服务自检
`permissionPresets=yes tools=yes sessions=yes`，设置页与接口均正常。

> 声明兼容不等于每个版本都做过完整实测。上表是支持范围，实际验证过的宿主版本见上方「已验证」。

- **工具清单**反映当前进程里可见的工具。被 `tool_policy` 收窄的团队成员看到更少，但拒绝规则照样生效 - **文件规则**只认得工具参数里的路径。shell 里 `rm`、`sed -i` 这类命令拿不到可靠路径—— 要彻底收死，请把 `bash` 剔除或整类拒绝 - **徽标**是在原生下拉里插入装饰节点实现的（DSH 的图标按固定 id 写死）。 DSH 若改版换了 DOM 结构，徽标可能不再显示——只是不显示，不影响功能 - **剔除**对当前轮的下一轮生效：工具清单在每轮开始时下发

为「让模型知道为什么不行」而写

**A permission studio for DSH** — turn three fixed tiers into any number of independently configured presets,
switchable mid-session

Four layers of control — categories, tools, commands, file paths — where every denial can tell the model what to do instead

[](https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases)
[](https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases/latest)
[](#development)
[](LICENSE)
[中文](README.md) · [English](README.en.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ---

DSH (DeepSeek Harness) ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-permission-presets`: any number of permission presets,
switchable mid-session with `/permission`. But the preset table can only be edited as YAML,
and its granularity stops at the **sandbox** (`read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`).

This plugin adds two things:

1. **A UI you can click** — add, edit and remove presets inside DSH Settings; saving takes effect immediately 2. **Finer-grained decisions** — from "sandbox on or off" down to *which kind of operation, which tool, which command, which file* The point: **a denial is not a dead end, it is an explanation.** Every rule can carry a message that is returned verbatim to the model, so it knows "this route is closed, take another" instead of retrying blindly.
File rules: each pattern sets read and write independently to allow / ask / deny, with an optional message

| Layer | Scope | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| **Categories** (13) | Bulk rules by operation type | "Always ask before running commands", "Never read outside the workspace" |
| **Per-tool** | One tool at a time, can be **removed** | "Make `bash` disappear from this session entirely" |
| **Regex rules** | Match tool name / command / path / arguments | "Always ask for `git push`", "Deny `rm -rf`" |
| **File rules** | By path, read and write judged separately | "Only `docs/**` is writable, `*.env` is never readable" |
Layers are checked top to bottom; the first match decides. **Within a layer, multiple matches resolve as deny > ask > allow.**

<table>
<tr><td width="50%" valign="top">

- Any number of tiers, each with its own sandbox and approval policy
- Display name, description, default flag
- Collapsible cards showing "deny N · ask M · 13 categories" at a glance
- Optional badge shown in Settings, the native dropdown and the composer trigger

13 operation types, each set to **ask / allow / deny**: shell commands · file reads · file search · file edits · reads outside the workspace · writes outside the workspace · images · network access · undo · subagents · teams · other tools · repeated calls

The tool list comes from the runtime registry (global layer plus every scoped layer),
**not a hardcoded list**. Each tool can be **follow category / ask / allow / deny / remove**.

**Remove** is not "deny at call time" — it uses DSH's `tools.restrict()` to take the tool out of this
session's visible surface, so the model never even receives its schema.
Recomputed on every preset switch: the old restriction is lifted before the new one is applied.
Match by tool name, command text, path or arbitrary arguments, with the same three actions. Higher priority than categories and per-tool overrides.

readme.section: File rules: allowlist and denylist are the same thing
readme.text:
- Set it to *allow* and it is an allowlist; set it to *deny* and it is a denylist — no two separate features
- Read and write are judged independently; **write does not imply read**
- Files not listed by any rule follow a separate fallback: follow the category rules (default, cannot lock you out)
  or deny everything (a pure allowlist)
- **The fallback still applies when the list is empty**: an empty list plus "deny everything" locks everything down,
  and the denial says why
- Dedicated "enable read" / "enable write" toggles, with warnings when either is missing
The page footer has three buttons: **Export backup / Import backup / Save all**.

- Export yields one JSON containing every preset: sandbox, approval, the thirteen rule categories, per-tool
  overrides, regex rules, file rules, icons and the default preset
- Export reflects the **current page state**, so you can export unsaved edits too
- Import replaces the whole preset set; the three built-in presets are always kept, and you get a confirmation
  prompt first
- Backups carry `format` and `formatVersion`; unrelated JSON, empty files and backups from a newer version are
  rejected with an explanation
Per-tool overrides: 48 tools discovered at runtime, bulk actions, removable

```sh
readme.section: Installing from the desktop app UI
readme.text:
The desktop profile is owned exclusively by the Electron app, so the CLI cannot touch it — use the UI:

**Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**, and paste:

```
https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio/releases/latest/download/dsh-permission-studio.tgz
```

readme.section: Installing from the desktop app UI
readme.text: That URL ends in `.tgz`, so the installer treats it as a tarball and you get the latest published release. **Do not paste the repository URL** (`https://github.com/zcr268/dsh-permission-studio`) — that installs from git and gives you whatever is on `main`, including unreleased commits. > Replace `desktop` with your profile name. List profiles with `dsh profile list`.

**Configure** → Settings → Permission presets → expand any preset **Switch** → `/permission` in a session (no argument lists every preset) ``` /permission 只碰指定文件 ``` Switching takes effect immediately, no restart. Badges follow the switch — the previous preset's icon does not linger.
Badges sit exactly where DSH's own icon would; built-in presets keep their native icons

Every denial can speak. Priority:

```
the rule's own message  >  the preset's fallback message  >  the category's default guidance
```

The fallback is resolved **at decision time**, not baked in when saving — change it once and every
entry that left its message blank follows immediately.

What the model receives is actionable, for example:

> This preset only allows paths listed in the file rules; `src/a.ts` is not listed. > Current rules: `docs/**`(read:allow write:allow), `*.md`(read:allow write:deny); > unlisted files follow "deny everything". Ask the user to adjust the file rules, or switch presets.

| Content | Location | |---|---| | Preset table, default preset | the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (native DSH config, hot-reloaded) | | Category / tool / regex / file rules, badges | `$DSH_HOME/permission-studio/config.json` | Stored separately on purpose: DSH does not know the shape of the fine-grained rules, and putting them into the native config would fail schema validation.

```
Settings iframe ──POST──> /permission-studio/api ──> write config ──> hot reload
                                                            │
every tool call ── tools/pre-execute (global hook) ──> decide()
        ├─ 1. regex rules (deny > ask > allow)

- `deny` → returns `{ kind: 'deny', reason }`; that reason is what the model reads
- `ask` → handed back to DSH's native approval, governed by the preset's approval policy
- plugin error → fail-safe denial, never a silent allow

| Method | Path | Purpose | |---|---|---| | GET | `/permission-studio/` | Self-contained page (inline HTML + CSS + JS) | | GET | `/permission-studio/api` | Presets, default, tool catalog, category enums | | POST | `/permission-studio/api` | Save all settings |

```sh
npm test          # 147 regression cases
npm pack          # build the tarball
```

Tests call the exported pure functions directly (`decide` / `matchFileRule` / `globToRegExp` /
`planHiddenTools` / `syncHiddenTools`); no server needed, runs in seconds.

Every bug that was fixed left a regression case behind — including a few non-obvious ones:

- `restrict` accumulates by intersection, so a preset switch must lift the old restriction or tools never come back - Badges that are only inserted and never removed end up side by side with the native icon after a switch - A fallback message materialized at save time stops responding to later edits - Treating "rules exist" as a precondition makes the fallback silently inert when the list is empty

Declared support (via `peerDependencies`):

| Package | Supported range |
|---|---|
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `>=4.0.2 <5.0.0` |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer` | `0.2.0-rc.1` · `0.2.0-rc.2` · `0.2.1-rc.1` · `0.2.1-rc.2` |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings` | same |
| `react` / `react-dom` | `^18.2.0` |
| Node.js | `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` |

Host-provided packages (cordis and the client UI packages) are not reinstalled into the profile,
so those peers are marked `optional` — no missing-peer warnings on install, while the range
stays an explicit promise.

Verified: installed and started on a clean `0.2.1-rc.2` host; service self-check reports
`permissionPresets=yes tools=yes sessions=yes`, and both the Settings page and the API respond.

> Declared compatibility is not a claim that every listed version was freshly tested.
> The table is the support range; the actually verified host is noted under "Verified".

- **The tool list** reflects tools visible in the current process. Team members narrowed by `tool_policy`
  see fewer, but deny rules still apply to them
- **File rules** only see paths passed as tool arguments. Shell commands like `rm` or `sed -i` carry no
  reliable path — to close that, remove `bash` or deny the whole category
- **Badges** are decoration nodes inserted into the native dropdown (DSH hardcodes its icons by preset id).
  If a DSH update changes that DOM, badges may stop appearing — display only, no functional impact
- **Removal** applies from the next turn of the current round; the tool surface is sent at the start of each turn

Built so the model knows why it cannot
